Senses.Explanation: The term names an observable walking circuit or action, with records specifying its timing, direction, companions, and coordination with rest. Literally, to 'go along walking' or 'walk about.' The term occurs 1,022 times in 273 allowed texts and names an observable bodily action. A late biography makes the direction explicit: at night a recluse goes outside the crag to walk about, the visiting master follows, and 'each walks east and west' (隱者出巖外經行，師亦隨之，第東西各步). A Five Lamps address pairs physical condition and action: 'when well, walk about; when tired, rest' (健即經行困即歇). The same collection records Layman Feng Ji walking about the teaching hall with Foyan when a child recites a line, and records another unnamed questioner 'walking under the pines one evening' when he hears a mountain spring (一夕，松下經行，聞巖泉聲). In the collected old cases, Sudhana searches in all four directions for seven days and finds Meghashri 'walking slowly on another peak' (在別峰上徐步經行). Daily timing is also explicit: a biography says an unnamed questioner ate only after serving the assembly, while Bingseng watched him 'walk about after each meal' (每飯罷經行時). The term is frequently coordinated with sitting and lying as one of the body's recorded activities. These places, times, directions, companions, and contrasts support the plain action word.
Senses.Note: All required definition formulas were searched; no stable nominal self-definition was found. Distinct deployment shapes retained are walking east-west at night, walking when well versus resting when tired, walking with another person in a hall, walking under pines, slow walking on another peak, and walking after a meal. The entry adds no special category beyond what the people in the records physically do.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄). Compiler narration reports an unnamed hermit walking outside the crag while the headed master follows.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword occurs in third-person narrative description rather than in speech by the person whose action is described.
